So last Friday (21/2/2025), three of us (mom, brother and me) was having our weekend trip to Batam.

We arrived at Batam Center Ferry Terminal at 9am local time. While lining up for passport check, I was setting up my roaming to fill up the Visa of Arrival (VOA). There, I was being called by an immigration lady to the office and both my mom’s and my phone, together with my passport was being taken by the immigration lady. Then, she told me to wait outside of her office (it was 9.30am Batam time). Roughly after 20-30 minutes, she went of of her office room to attend another offencer, but when she saw me, she asked me “kamu ngapain disini?” twice because I was super clueless. Then I told her that my phone and passport was taken by her. She then rudely told me “ha tahu pun kamu, kamu tahu nggak apa salahmu?” I replied, “aku tadi lagi setting my roaming service to fill my VOA”. Then, she told me that roaming can be done after immigration outside. I then just remained silent and nod softly. She then went back into her room and ghosted me for not sure how many hours. While waiting for her action, I was just sat on the chair, not provoking nor asking for a release because I believe she just did her job. Then, there was a man sat right to me asking what happened. I told him that my passport and phones were taken by the officer. He then softly told me that he can offer help. Me being suspicious with the offer (I can sense that his help came with a tipping/side money, I replied him “nggak papa. Aku tunggu aja”). This man then left me and went for another offender (not directly but periodically he will come into the room).

Bear in mind that throughout my wait, there were many offender after me that being released in less than 10 minutes waiting (one of them directly was with the guy who offered me help).

Fast forward, I was being held in the waiting area, from 9am until 1.30pm. When I was about to be released, the lady officer told me to not use phone anymore while waiting for the immigration check. Me being frustrated being held that long without phone and passport, replied her with a single word, “maybe”. She got furious and proceed to reject my entry. I told her that “that’s okay. Just send me back to Malaysia cause I was mentally and physically drained from the wait”.

While waiting for my return ferry, she came to me asking me to call my family. Apparently, when my ferry PIC informed my mom that I will be sent home for “rude” behaviour, my mum was asking the lady officer’s name from the ferry PIC, and wanted to report her for wrong accussation. I was being accused for playing my phone despite being warned twice by the other officer (in which, I was not being warned at all for the offense (if any). She then cleared my entry after hearing that my mom wanted to report her for possible act of corruption and misaccusation (because at 11.30am Batam time, my mom went into the waiting area to see me, and I told her that there was one local guy offered me for help). The last picture was the guy who offered me help, having a conversation with the lady officer.

This posting was not to accuse the officer for act of corruption, but for the visitor to be more aware of this frequent incidences of “random check/using phone while in immigration” offense. Also, for the public authority to investigate the presence of the guy offering me help in the Batam Center Ferry Immigration office. Why were he in the office most of the time. Also to Ms Cia, you owed me my 4 hours time waiting like a stupid guy, and you don’t deserve my respect.

text:
Hey guys, it’s your favorite elite traveler back with another unfiltered review—and this time, we need to talk about the gatekeeping situation at the Batam Center Ferry Terminal.

As an Indonesian who travels extensively, I am usually so proud to welcome international visitors to our beautiful country. But my recent arrival at Batam Center at 9:30 PM was, without exaggeration, an absolute NIGHTMARE. If this terminal is meant to be a major international gateway, the current reality is a total embarrassment to our national hospitality.

Here is the raw truth about what you can expect if you land here late at night:

1. The Immigration Bottle-Neck (The Absolute Worst Part)
Imagine an entire ferry of exhausted travelers arriving at 9:30 PM, only to find exactly one immigration officer working the counter. The inefficiency was mind-boggling.

But the real vibe-killer was the officer handling the desk—an older woman named Ibu May. To say she was rude is an understatement. Unprofessional, highly inefficient, and frankly, throwing what I can only describe as a 5-year-old’s tantrum behind the desk. As an Indonesian, it broke my heart to watch her. She is single-handedly ruining the image of Indonesian hospitality for every international tourist standing in that excruciatingly long line.

2. Zero Digital Readiness
Before you even get to the chaos inside, there is no coordination at the entrance. There are no QR codes shared or displayed at the entrance for required digital arrivals or health forms before you enter the terminal. Everyone is left scrambling in the dark, trying to figure out what they need to do. It’s clunky, outdated, and unacceptable for a major transit hub in 2026.

3. The Transport Monopoly Trap
Once you finally escape the terminal, don't even think about opening your Grab or Gojek apps. The terminal strictly bans ride-hailing apps to protect their local taxi monopoly.

Normally, I’m all for supporting local drivers, but the execution here is a safety and logistical hazard. Most of the drivers stationed there are very elderly, struggle to understand directions, and—unbelievably—do not know how to type into or use Google Maps to reach your destination. If you don't know the exact streets yourself, you are essentially stranded with a driver who can't navigate.

The Verdict 🚨
Batam Center Ferry Terminal needs a massive wake-up call, urgent staff retraining, and a complete tech overhaul. To the management: please address the lack of personnel, the attitude of staff like Ibu May, and let ride-hailing apps in so travelers can actually get home safely.

text:
Batam Centre Point International Ferry Terminal - Functional But Basic
Location: Batam Centre, Kota Batam, Kepulauan Riau
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐ (3.5/5)
I've passed through this terminal several times over the past year, so I've gotten pretty familiar with how it operates.
The Good:
The basics are covered well enough. There are plenty of SIM card kiosks right when you arrive, which is handy if you need to get connected immediately. Immigration processing is straightforward - nothing fancy, but it moves along at a reasonable pace. Luggage retrieval is simple and easy to navigate.
The real bonus is the overhead walkway that connects directly to Mega City Mall. Makes getting to the Grab taxi stand super convenient - you don't have to deal with touts or figure out where to go. Just walk across and you're there.
The Not-So-Good:
It's a functional terminal, but that's about it. Don't expect much in terms of amenities or comfort while you're waiting. The facility feels pretty basic and could use some updating to make the arrival/departure experience more pleasant.
Bottom Line:
Does the job for getting in and out of Batam, and the connection to Mega City Mall is genuinely useful for onward travel. It's not going to wow you, but it won't give you major headaches either. If you're a regular traveler to Batam like me, you'll appreciate the straightforward layout even if it's nothing special. Sonnet 4.5

text:
CORRUPT IMMIGRATION OFFICERS AT THIS FERRY TERMINAL IMMIGRATION

On 21 February, my family and I made a plan to visit Batam, Indonesia. The Chinese New Year holiday had just passed, and we wanted a short, peaceful getaway—two days of rest and sightseeing before my mother returns to the Philippines. It was meant to be simple family time.

We are Philippine passport holders - husband, myself and my daughter have valid SG long term pass. Indonesians grant 30-day visa-free entry for Philippine passport holders. We had return tickets within the allowed period. We had hotel bookings. Everything was straightforward.

But the moment we reached immigration in Batam on 21 Feb 2026, 1030AM Indonesian time, things changed.

We were suddenly held back and questioned. The officers accused us of traveling to Batam “only to extend my mom’s visa in Singapore.” This accusation shocked us. Why would Indonesian immigration be concerned about Singapore’s ICA policies? We were entering Indonesia legally under Indonesia’s visa-free scheme. We were not overstaying anywhere. We were not violating any Indonesian law.

Despite explaining that this was a short 2-day leisure trip, we were escorted into an office for further “interrogation.”

The room was poorly lit and tense. There were other tourists inside as well, including an Indian passport holder who also appeared distressed. The atmosphere felt intimidating. Questions were repeated. The tone was accusatory, as if we had already done something wrong.

Then the officer’s tone changed.
He told us we had “two options”:
1. Change my mother’s flight and book her a ticket back to the Philippines on a date they wanted.
2. Pay SGD 150 as a “penalty” for “transiting” in Batam.

Penalty for what violation? There was no clear explanation. No written notice. No official receipt mentioned upfront. No formal charge. Just two “options.”

Why should Indonesian immigration dictate when my mother flies back to the Philippines? Why was there a “penalty” when we were within Indonesia’s visa-free entry rules?

At that moment, fear took over. We were in a foreign immigration office. We saw how the officer spoke to other tourists. We did not know what could happen next—would they deny entry? Cancel our passports? Blacklist us? Create further complications for our travel?

Feeling intimidated and powerless, and wanting to avoid further trouble, we agreed to pay the money.

What was supposed to be a relaxing family trip turned into a deeply stressful and unsettling experience. It leaves travelers questioning:
1. Are short leisure trips now suspicious?
2. Is visiting Batam after staying in Singapore automatically treated as wrongdoing?
3. Why are tourists pressured with vague “penalties” without clear written violations?

Experiences like this damage trust. Tourism thrives on safety, fairness, and transparency. When travelers feel intimidated or pressured without clear legal basis, it creates fear—not confidence.

We came for rest and sightseeing. We left with disappointment.

This will likely be our last visit to Batam.

To fellow travelers: always keep your documents complete, know your visa rules, and stay calm—but also be aware of your rights. No holiday should begin with fear.
